solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: For transplant, scan iris and other flowers

indicators.note: to transplant is to move something into a new position, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener moving plants sets aside a scan of irises before shifting the other blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For transplant' signals that SCAN and IRIS are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi (daffodils and their kin) are spring flowers other than the iris.

clue.text: Face operation: expert does, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is to be taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: an expert knows the job

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon's work on the face, which only an expert can do.
explanation.walkthrough: An expert 'knows (the) job', and KNOWS JOB said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is informal for rhinoplasty, cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose, a facial operation.

clue.text: Right oven, for this?

parts.note: an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Is this the proper oven to cook a joint in?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an oven is right for a roast. An oast is the kiln in a hop-drying oast house of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is meat cooked in an oven, so the right oven is for exactly this dish.

clue.text: Unconcerned to be popular, standing out from the crowd?

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
something that stands out from the crowd is different

explanation.surface: It is hard to care about being liked when you are the odd one out.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifferent means having no interest or concern, the same as unconcerned.

clue.text: Shore leave in hopeless place

definitions.meaning: to leave them stuck with no way out

explanation.surface: Sailors on shore leave end up stuck in a dismal port.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is literary for a beach, and stranding someone abandons them helpless, as a ship left aground.

clue.text: Abbreviated state service

definitions.meaning: .... is the short form of Massachusetts, a US state
the central church service of Catholic worship

explanation.surface: A government department gives a cut-down version of its public service.
explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts is shortened in writing to Mass., and the Mass is a church service, the Eucharist.

clue.text: Tiny workers' high-rise accommodation

parts.note: worker ants are tiny workers, and their heaped mound of a nest rises high

explanation.surface: It sounds like a tower block for low-paid staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny workers' suggests underpaid people; it means insects in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill is the mound built by ants over their nest, a tall home for worker insects.

clue.text: Second shopping area is modest

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A town's second shopping centre is nothing grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and modest both describe something limited in size or scale.

clue.text: Good man meets with resistance

parts.note: ST, short for saint, a good man
with means together with, and

explanation.surface: A decent fellow comes up against opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a stand is to put up resistance, so a stand is an act of opposing.

clue.text: Cheese and some apricot taken

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snack of cheese with a bit of apricot on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Stupidly censorious about name for man of taste

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
stupidly means foolishly put together, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic is foolishly harsh about a cultured man's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' mixes up CENSORIOUS, and 'about' wraps those letters round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur is an expert judge of matters of taste, such as food, wine or art.

clue.text: Judge turned to note

indicators.note: turned means the little word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A judge turns to a written note in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To jot is to note down quickly; both are verbs for writing a brief record.

clue.text: Money's problematic if in a clan

definitions.note: read as an adjective, 'money's' means of or about money

indicators.note: something problematic is in a mess, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A clan's money troubles come down to one word: if.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial means relating to money or funds, as 'money's' does when read possessively.

clue.text: Dairy product from goat?

definitions.meaning: a goat butts with its head, so it is one that butts

explanation.surface: Asking where a dairy product comes from: could it be a goat?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke reading: a goat is a 'butter' because it butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter is churned from cream; a goat, known for ramming with its horns, is whimsically one that butts.

clue.text: Too shy to play piano in store

indicators.note: to play with letters is to move them about freely, so they come out in a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A child too timid to play the piano in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A toyshop is a store selling toys.

clue.text: Almost become unable to see mischievous spirit

parts.note: to go can mean to become, as in go mad

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: blind means unable to see

explanation.surface: A sprite nearly loses its sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the last letter from GO BLIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is an ugly, impish creature of folklore that plays tricks on people.

clue.text: Close match, one assumed after dark

parts.note: nigh means near, close
a tie is a match, as a cup tie in football

explanation.surface: A tight contest, with one side's victory taken for granted as night fell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed' here means put on, as clothes are; a cup tie is a knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment put on at bedtime.

clue.text: A change involving one in birdcage

indicators.note: involving means the change word takes the numeral into itself

parts.note: to vary is to change
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone alters the arrangement inside a cage for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure or cage where birds are kept.

clue.text: Insect takes off from pages of book

parts.note: a fly is an insect
leaves means departs, takes off

explanation.surface: An insect flits off from the pages of a book it was resting on.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyleaves are the blank sheets at the front and back of a bound volume.

clue.text: See me wrapped up in warm coat, but only part of leg

indicators.note: wrapped means the coat goes round the other piece

parts.note: a fur is a warm coat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word me is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bundled in a warm coat, only part of my leg shows.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' reads a word from the bottom, so the two-letter word is turned; 'wrapped' then sets the coat round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the upper part of the leg.

clue.text: Drinking bout in front half of car

indicators.note: front half means only the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: a Jaguar is a make of car

explanation.surface: A boozing session takes place in the front of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A jag is a spell of unrestrained indulgence, especially a drinking spree.

clue.text: Leap year makes us nervous

parts.note: to jump is to leap

explanation.surface: The prospect of a leap year makes people jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpy describes someone anxious and easily startled, as a nervous person is.

clue.text: Sage parent accepts head covering

indicators.note: accepts means the parent takes the hat in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: mama is a word for mother, a parent
a hat covers the head

explanation.surface: A wise parent agrees to wear a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, meaning great soul, is an Indian title for a revered wise person, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Cornish tourist came across me, back at the front

indicators.note: at the front places that turned word before the other piece
back means the word me is turned to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
met means came across, encountered

explanation.surface: A visitor to Cornwall bumped into me and then pushed in at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a holiday county in south-west England, whose locals have their own dialect name for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet, a dialect word for ant, is what Cornish locals call holiday visitors.

clue.text: Ready to eat? Tear back from office

parts.note: to rip is to tear

indicators.note: back from means the letter at the rear of office is picked

explanation.surface: A worker hurries back from the office, hungry for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is ripe has matured fully and can be eaten.

clue.text: Good for food, for example, which a poet might use?

definitions.text: Good for food, for example, which a poet might use?

parts.words: Good for food, for example, which a poet might use?
parts.note: good and food are spelt alike at the end but sound different, a pairing a poet may use for the look of it

explanation.surface: It reads like advice on healthy eating, then turns into a question about poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good for food' looks like praise of a meal; it is the pair of words GOOD and FOOD, which match on the page but not when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye rhyme pairs words spelt alike but pronounced differently, like good and food, rhyming only to the sight.
